cells.tense: The shape shows itself, and you are here with the pen, choosing it.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Pick what you actually want from this and point your next hour at it, plainly.
cells.core:
You see the shape under things, and you can tell the difference between a shape that frees you and one that just looks tidy. That is not cleverness for its own sake. It is a working understanding, and it is doing what it's for — you catch how a situation actually works early enough to steer, and you steer. What you choose tends to hold, because you chose it out of what you could see.

The pull toward what you want is real and it is pointing somewhere, and this week you can put a name on where it is going. Not a plan. Choose the want you would be sorriest to lose, say it plainly to yourself, and make one turn toward it — the call, the first page, the appointment. Let the pull do some of the walking instead of only the reading.

cells.tense: You will have already patterned a future you cannot yet write in, and braced against it.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Give it one small container — a date, a list, a place the thing lives — so there is a shape in your hands.
cells.core:
Where you see the shape under things, it's now seeing past the point you can act on. The patterns arrive before the events do, and each one has a next shape behind it, so the analysis has no floor. That isn't a flaw in you; it's the same skill running without a place to land, and from the inside it feels like diligence. The shape keeps predicting, and you keep bracing.

What settles it is building one small container and putting it down. Not the whole architecture — one date, one list, one place the thing lives. A shape you can carry keeps you here with it, and the predicting tends to stop when there is something in your hands.

cells.tense: The door was already behind you when you turned to look at it, and you are still standing there.
cells.act: join the practice the others keep
cells.ask: Join one practice the people you trust keep — show up once, the way they do it, and ask nothing of the visit.
cells.core:
Where you see what's under things, you've stopped seeing past the surface now. What's here is what's here, and no more — a symbol is just a shape, a habit is just a habit, and there is nothing underneath to find.

Depth comes back through other people, not through effort. Find one thing the people near you actually keep — the weekly dinner, the walk, the way they mark the end of a season — and join it once, exactly as they do it, without improving it or asking it for anything. You'll feel the pull of it before you understand it. That's the point.

cells.tense: The pen is down on the table, and you are already writing in a room you haven't looked at.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: Next time someone close is in it, sit with them without fixing it, and keep your own footing while you do.
cells.core:
You read patterns well enough that other people feel read, and you've been doing it without knowing you do it. In a conversation, you find the shape of what's wrong for the other person before they've said it — and you take it on, adjust to it, carry it. That's the skill working. What's missing is that you don't see the moment you crossed into it, so you leave yourself behind and don't notice going.

What brings you back is contact that keeps both sides — being with someone in what they're carrying without fixing it, and staying your own size while you do. You'll feel the pull to merge, name it silently, and stay. That's not coldness. That's two people in a room.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: none of the four cores correctly names the partner's mechanism, but the Too Much ask leans on the record's diagonal (Authority) which the record does support. The reader could reasonably object that 'pattern-seeing' in the Too Much cell describes anyone who's ever been anxious, and that the Too Little cell says where the person stands but not why — which is allowed. The ask survives being wrong: if the person can't find a moment where they were braced against a future, the act of putting one small container on the mess is still useful. The sentence that serves the writer more than them: 'seeing how things work beneath surface appearance' — it quotes the record and would look good on a poster; I'm not using it. I'm struck by how narrow the gap is between the pattern that frees and the pattern that traps — the Abstraction at Fruition in Will is one card that can close or open depending on whether the person is steering by it or it is steering them.
